title: Customer network kickoff + TF simplify playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic kickoff + simplification playbook for onboarding enterprise customers into Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). The doc focuses on two parallel tracks: the customer network onboarding kickoff checklist and an internal refactor of our TF modules/state layout to reduce drift and speed upgrades. Draft notes, TODOs, and quick commands are mixed in — this is intentionally rough.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target: mid-size to large enterprise with dedicated VPC (single-region) and optional on-prem edge.
- We assume customer will provide: BGP peering parameters OR VPN termination config, CIDR ranges, KMS endpoint information, and an inventory of internal IP allowlists.
- This playbook is NOT a final runbook for airgapped installations (separate doc).

Kickoff checklist (customer-facing, run during first 1–2 calls):
1) Pre-kickoff packet sent (48h prior): short questionnaire for CIDRs, preferred regions, compliance controls, and contact list. Template: <= 1 page.
2) Network diagram sketch: customer internet edge -> transit VPC -> Redwood ingress VPC -> customer-private-subnets (examples below). Get initial CIDR acceptance.
3) SSH/IP allowlist: collect jump/proxy IPs and define access windows.
4) Certificate/KMS: confirm if customer wants to use their KMS (HSM) or Redwood-managed keys. If customer KMS, get IAM policies.
5) TF state preferences: customer-managed state (remote backend) vs Redwood-managed state. NOTE: prefer remote state for private installs to avoid large state migrations later.
6) SLA/Escalation: share SRE on-call rotation and expected RTO for onboarding incidents.

Minimal acceptance diagram (text):
- Transit (customer) --[VPN/BGP]--> Redwood Transit VPC (shared infra) --[VPC peering/PrivateLink]--> Customer tenant VPC hosting Redwood runtime.
- For on-prem, transit represented by SD-WAN appliance -> customer-edge-router -> peering to Redwood transit.

Terraform refactor notes (internal):
Goal: make TF modules more composable across customer topologies and reduce duplication during upgrades. Key points and migration path.
- Module split suggestion:
  - network/core: creates transit VPC, shared route tables, and baseline IAM
  - network/tenant: per-customer VPC, subnets, security groups, endpoint interfaces
  - infra/peering: peering + route propagation resources isolated so replacing peering logic has minimal blast radius
  - secrets/kms: wrapper module around KMS keys and policies (supports BYOK)
- Naming strategy: use stable logical names: redwood-<customer>-tenant-vpc, redwood-<customer>-transit, redwood-<customer>-efs etc. Avoid embedding numeric suffixes where avoidable.
- Variables: prefer structured flat variables (strings & lists) over maps-of-maps to keep plan/apply diffs readable. Example: var subnets = ["10.10.0.0/24", "10.10.1.0/24"] rather than complex map.
- State migration plan (high level):
  1) Create new backend for new module layout (s3/remote with locking).
  2) Import existing real resources into new module state using terraform import per resource id. Keep a running mapping sheet (spreadsheet linked in CON-4821).
  3) Run plan with -target to reconcile the new modules only.
  4) Small batch migration: 1–3 customers per week for the first month.
- Backwards compatibility: modules must accept legacy inputs for 2 release cycles; add validations to warn on deprecated params.

Upgrade and rolling deploy plan (customer tenant VPC changes and runtime upgrades):
- Objectives: zero-or-minimal downtime, predictable routing during kernel/instance upgrades, reversible steps.
- High-level pattern: blue/green-like networking: create new ASGs/instances in same VPC but different subnets/targets, warm caches, switch traffic via load-balancer DNS or route table modification.
- Steps for control-plane upgrade with minimal disruption:
  1) Validate health checks and readiness probes on staging images.
  2) Start 20% of new capacity in tenant VPC (warm).
  3) Gradually shift traffic using LB weight or route priorities (5–10% increments).
  4) Monitor token latency, KPIs, and error rates. Roll back if error rate > 1% over 5 minutes.
- Network-specific upgrades (route changes, peering updates): perform during low-traffic windows, preflight with traceroutes and BGP route dumps. Have rollback plan to restore previous route tables.

Preflight tests (minimum):
- From customer bastion: curl health endpoints for each service and run a 30-second generation load (sample prompt).
- Tracepath to model-serving endpoints, ensure expected path hits Redwood transit (confirm via next-hop).
- Verify KV/cache warming by issuing sequential requests that should hit cache (observe lower latencies).

Common pitfalls & notes to self:
- Customers often reuse small CIDR pools; insist on unique tenant CIDRs early.
- Buried dependency: some customer egress proxies terminate TLS and block mutual TLS to model-backend; confirm certificate passthrough requirements.
- TF gotcha: changing a subnet's availability zone can recreate resources. Prefer AZ-agnostic module designs where possible.

Runbook excerpts (quick commands):
- Verify peering: aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=requester-vpc-info.vpc-id,Values=<vpc-id>
- Check route tables: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc-id>
- Terraform import example: terraform import module.network.module.tenant.aws_vpc.customer_vpc vpc-0abcd1234

Open questions (to decide on kickoff):
- Do we require customers to accept provider-side Flow Logs for initial onboarding? (privacy/legal may object)
- Default MTU settings for SD-WAN customers — use 1500 or 9001? Note: jumbo MTU can break path MTU discovery on legacy appliances.

Acceptance criteria for onboarding completion:
- Control plane: all Redwood services report healthy from customer bastion and from Redwood SRE probes.
- Performance: median token latency <= agreed SLO during baseline synthetic test.
- Security: customer KMS access validated and audit logs flowing for initial 7 days.
- Terraform: all resources managed in target backend with no drift alerts for 48 hours.

Next actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Draft short customer packet and send to sales/solutions for review (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Create GH PR to split terraform-modules (owner: Ethan) — start with network/core and network/tenant. See PR 142 for prototype.
- [ ] Schedule dry-run migration with internal staging tenant (owner: Priya) week of 2025-03-03.

Appendix: quick-example TF snippet (intent only)
```hcl
module "tenant" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//network/tenant?ref=modular-2025-alpha"
  name   = "redwood-acme-tenant"
  cidrs  = ["10.20.0.0/22"]
  public_subnets  = ["10.20.0.0/24"]
  private_subnets = ["10.20.1.0/24"]
}
```
(End of draft)
